column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly describes Abijah’s army as mighty warriors as well as chosen men; BSB expresses the first description only for Jeroboam’s men.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says sons; BSB uses descendants.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains sons of worthlessness and a soft heart and repeats strengthening; BSB uses wicked men, inexperienced, and resisting.
The Hebrew has singular hand and sons of David; BSB uses plural hands and descendants. The Hebrew calls the multitude large without explicitly calling it an army.
The Hebrew retains filling his hand; BSB renders this consecrating himself.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats morning and evening and explicitly retains keeping the charge; BSB uses every morning and evening and carrying out the requirements.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has a plural subject before Judah; BSB identifies this as singular he.
The Hebrew has behold where BSB says discovered.
The Hebrew repeats men of Judah; BSB uses they for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew says sons of Israel and singular hand; BSB uses Israelites and plural hands.
The Hebrew repeats striking as verb and noun; BSB uses struck with a mighty blow.
The Hebrew says sons of Israel and sons of Judah; BSB uses Israelites and men of Judah.
The Hebrew repeats daughters after each city; BSB combines them as their villages.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has an active begetting verb; BSB says became the father.
The Hebrew calls the record an inquiry or exposition; BSB uses Treatise.
